payload: {"note": "d04 Fri 07:19: dish_rack_k1 held pot_1; resident_2 present. My forecast missed pot_1 (P=0.05) and over-predicted plates/pan. P(pot_1|dish_rack_k1) is high, not low. P(plate_1|dish_rack_k1) and P(plate_2|dish_rack_k1) are low when pot_1 is present. P(pan_1|dish_rack_k1) is low. resident_2 is active in kitchen.", "fork": {"beliefs": "The household operates on a 'personal territory' model for personal items (bedrooms/persons), but shared kitchen items follow a 'function-based' model. Dish_rack_k1 is the primary location for clean or drying cookware (pot_1, pan_1) and plates, not just a random drop zone. Counter_k1 is the active prep/drop zone for food items and personal carry-alls (backpacks, water bottles, wallets) during morning routines. Sink_k1 is a secondary drop zone for small personal items (mugs, wallets) and dirty dishes. The presence of resident_2 in the kitchen strongly correlates with items being on counter_k1 or sink_k1, not necessarily dish_rack_k1, unless they are specifically drying. Personal items rarely appear in shared spaces unless temporarily moved for immediate use or dropped during transit. Entry area remains the primary drop zone for keys/jackets upon arrival. Bedroom floors are for jackets/backpacks upon entering the bedroom. Nightstands are for phones/chargers at night. Desks are for laptops/notebooks during work. If an object is missing from its owner's bedroom, it is likely ON_PERSON, OUT_OF_HOUSE, or in a shared space if the owner is currently active there.", "why": "Previous beliefs treated shared spaces as generic drop zones, leading to poor forecasts for specific kitchen receptacles like dish_rack_k1. The look at dish_rack_k1 revealed pot_1, confirming it as a specific location for cookware, not just any item. This refines the model to distinguish between active prep (counter), washing/drying (sink/dish_rack), and personal drop-offs (sink/counter). This functional distinction improves probability assignments for kitchen objects."}}
